judgment.rationale: Both Indicators sit in BASIC 4, Strand 1 NUMBER, Sub-strand 3 Fractions (rank 0 for both), so direction rests on statement substance rather than coordinate gap. B4.1.3.1.1 (second) has learners generate unit fractions and locate a unit fraction on a number line by partitioning 0-1 into equal parts, with LCs 'Generate unit fractions' and 'Locate a unit fraction on a number line ... partitioning it into equal parts'; this establishes part-whole meaning and fraction magnitude. B4.1.3.2.1 (first) requires comparing and ordering fractions with like denominators via pictorial representations and equivalent fractions found with the LCD, which presupposes the ability to construct and place unit fractions and interpret their size. Proficiency with the unit-fraction/number-line work therefore supports success in comparing and ordering, giving a same-rank second-to-second-order developmental direction from the second SFI to the first. Note the Basic 4 Fractions code anomaly in the parent Content Standards (B4.1.3.1 kept separate, B4.1.3.2 merged from a mislabelled row); this affects code interpretation only, not the substantive skill relation, and the two SFIs' own source excerpts are complete and non-conflicting despite truncated source-evidence lists.

Audit context confirms these are distinct source-visible items with different official codes and grade scopes rather than a merge artifact, so the recurrence is a genuine cross-grade reiteration of the same rounding skill. Because the indicator text, number range (100,000), and target place values are identical, the evidence shows no substantive deepening, extension, or increased complexity at this grain to justify a lower-to-higher buildsTowards claim; the parent Content Standards differ in scope (up to 1,000,000 vs up to 1 billion) but that is ancestor context only and cannot serve as endpoint evidence. This is therefore meaningful reinforcement/coherence of the same skill across BASIC 5 and BASIC 6 rather than a developmental dependency. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted source-evidence items each) and all endpoints and ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, so any finer grade-specific differentiation in the full source is not visible here.

judgment.rationale: Both Indicators sit under the same BASIC 5 Algebra Content Standard B5.2.1.1 ('Determine the pattern rule to make predictions about subsequent elements') and share the same resolved grade coordinate (BASIC 5, rank 1), so direction rests on substantive content rather than rank. B5.2.1.1.1 (second SFI) has learners extend a given pattern with and without concrete materials and explain how each element differs from the preceding one — informal, concrete identification and verbalisation of the element-to-element change. B5.2.1.1.7 (first SFI) requires writing that rule both in words and in algebraic (symbolic) form for a given pattern. Proficiency in detecting and articulating the difference between successive elements is the substantive basis for formalising that regularity as a stated and then symbolic rule, an increase in abstraction and representational demand; the shared LC token 'pattern' plus the complementary LC sets ('extend'/'explain' vs 'rule in words'/'rule in algebra') support this reading. Both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context and truncated source evidence (24 omitted evidence items each), so the judgment rests on the bounded statement text, LCs, and hierarchy shown; the merge notes only distinguish these Basic 5 items from identically worded Basic 6 items and do not contradict the reading.
